[EVALUATION RESULT]
Question: Let $G$ be a primitive permutation group, acting on a set $\Omega$, with socle $\mathrm{PSU}(3,q)$, where $q=p^m\ge 7$ for an odd prime $p$, and let $M$ be a point stabilizer of $G$ containing $\mathrm{PSO}(3,q)$. (Here $b(G)$ denotes the base size of $G$, i.e. the minimum size of a subset $\Delta\subseteq\Omega$ whose pointwise stabilizer $G_{(\Delta)}$ is trivial, and $\mathbb Z_{m_1}$ denotes a cyclic group of order $m_1$.) Which description gives the complete list of possible pairs $(G,M)$ together with the value of the base size $b(G)$?
Predicted label: 'C'
Predicted text: 'One has $b(G)=2$, and exactly two possibilities occur: either $G=\\mathrm{PSU}(3,q)$ and $M=\\mathrm{SO}(3,q)$, or $G=\\mathrm{PSU}(3,q)\\,\\mathbb Z_{m_1}$ and $M=\\mathrm{SO}(3,q)\\,\\mathbb Z_{m_1}$ for some $m_1$ dividing $2m$ with $m_1\\ne 1$; conversely, every such divisor $m_1$ actually occurs.'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: 'One has $b(G)=2$, and exactly two possibilities occur: either $G=\\mathrm{PSU}(3,q)$ and $M=\\mathrm{SO}(3,q)$, or $G=\\mathrm{PSU}(3,q)\\,\\mathbb Z_{m_1}$ and $M=\\mathrm{SO}(3,q)\\,\\mathbb Z_{m_1}$ for some $m_1$ dividing $2m$ with $m_1\\ne 1$.'
Exact Match: 0.0
